# Railroad diagram syntax (ABNF)

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-railroad/grammar/railroad-abnf.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Railroad diagram syntax, ABNF notation (R-PARSE-9, D54, D512): the normative grammar of
`railroad-abnf-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/abnf/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a
reference parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it.
mermaid@12 decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this
file (DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed the ABNF notation with Langium (`railroad-abnf.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`, which does not import `common.langium`); the rules below are its token
rules, in its order, and its grammar. The other notations have grammars of their own
(`railroad.ebnf`, `railroad-ebnf.ebnf`, `railroad-peg.ebnf`).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

`;` ends a rule only at the end of its line: followed by anything else on its line, a blank
too, it starts a comment to the line end, as in mermaid@12 (D513). A name is letters, digits
and `-` (no `_`), and a string has no escapes. A name that starts with `title` reads as a
`title` line. Line breaks are blanks.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `railroad-abnf-beta`, then `title`, `accTitle` and `accDescr` lines, then rules.
The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE`, `COMMENT` and `SEMI_COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped before
parsing.

```ebnf
abnf = Header { text } { Rule } EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = HEADER ;
```

```ebnf
text = Title
     | AccTitle
     | AccDescr ;
```

`name = … ;`: a rule, drawn as a track from its name. A name defined twice is drawn
twice.

```ebnf
Rule @Rule = ID EQUALS alternation SEMI ;
```

Alternatives, one of which is taken; one alternative is itself.

```ebnf
alternation = concatenation { SLASH concatenation } ;
```

Elements one after another; one element is itself.

```ebnf
concatenation = element { element } ;
```

An element and how often it repeats: `0*1` and `*1` make it optional.

```ebnf
element = [ REPEAT | EXACT_REPEAT ] primary ;
```

```ebnf
primary = STRING
        | NUM_VAL
        | ID
        | LPAREN alternation RPAREN
        | LBRACKET alternation RBRACKET ;
```

`title Grammar`: the title (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | HEADER | `railroad-abnf-beta(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `railroad-abnf-beta`: starts a railroad diagram in the ABNF notation, followed by a blank, a line break or `%%`. |
| INITIAL | EQUALS | `=` |  | `=` between a rule's name and its definition. |
| INITIAL | SEMI_COMMENT | `;[^\n\r]+` |  | `;` and the rest of its line, when the line goes on: a comment. mermaid@12 tries it as the longer alternative of `;`, so it is listed first. |
| INITIAL | SEMI | `;` |  | `;` at the end of a line: the end of a rule. |
| INITIAL | SLASH | `\/` |  | `a / b`: one of the alternatives. |
| INITIAL | LPAREN | `\(` |  | `( … )`: a group, drawn as its contents. |
| INITIAL | RPAREN | `\)` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LBRACKET | `\[` |  | `[ … ]`: optional contents: a bypass above. |
| INITIAL | RBRACKET | `\]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the diagram's title, the rest of the line (quotes around it are dropped). It is not drawn. |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ID | `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*` |  | A rule's name: a letter, then letters, digits and `-`. A name in an expression is a reference to that rule, drawn in a square box. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"[^"]*"` |  | `"…"`: literal text, drawn in a rounded box as written (no escapes). |
| INITIAL | NUM_VAL | `%[xXdDbB][0-9A-Fa-f]+(?:[-.][0-9A-Fa-f]+)*` |  | `%x41`, `%d65-90`, `%b1.0.1`: a value in hexadecimal, decimal or binary, with a range or a list, drawn as written. |
| INITIAL | REPEAT | `[0-9]*\*[0-9]*` |  | `n*m` before an element: `n` to `m` times (`*` alone: any number, `1*`: once or more, `*1`: at most once). Only whether `n` is 0 shows in the drawing. |
| INITIAL | EXACT_REPEAT | `[0-9]+` |  | `n` before an element: exactly `n` times. |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t \r\n]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
